page: Microsoft Azure D64ls_v5 is a compute-optimized virtual machine belonging to the DLSv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The x86_64 architecture is supported by a cache hierarchy consisting of 48 KB L1d, 1 MB L2, and 48 MB L3 cache. The system is configured with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include any local storage or bundled GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

In benchmark evaluations, the D64ls_v5 demonstrates strong multi-core performance. It achieves top-tier results in stress-ng multi-core CPU tests, Geekbench multi-core scores, and Passmark CPU evaluations, including extended instructions, encryption, and physics tests. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient for large blocks, with uncached read speeds reaching 292.88 GB/sec and write speeds at 135.25 GB/sec. Single-core performance, single-threaded compression, and Redis SET operations fall within the average tier. Large-scale LLM text generation is a notable bottleneck, performing in the bottom tier due to the lack of hardware acceleration.

Given its low-memory configuration of 2.0 GB per core and absence of local storage, the D64ls_v5 offers a cost-efficient profile for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints or local disk caching. It is highly suited for multi-threaded tasks such as software compilation, ray tracing, image processing, and static web serving. It also performs well for database operations when paired with external premium storage, though it is less optimal for memory-bound applications or large-scale AI model inference.

It features 64 dedicated vCPUs (32 physical cores) and 128.0 GB of RAM, translating to a low-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. Running on Microsoft Hyper-V, this server lacks local storage and GPUs but is Premium Storage capable. Benchmarks indicate strong multi-core CPU performance, high memory bandwidth for large blocks, and excellent throughput in software compilation, ray tracing, and static web serving. Conversely, single-core execution and large-scale LLM inference are average to weak. The D64ls_v5 is highly cost-efficient for compute-intensive, multi-threaded workloads such as CI/CD pipelines, image processing, and database operations that rely on external storage rather than massive memory footprints.
